html:
The ancient Christian church of Ethiopia, one of the oldest in the world, with tens of millions of members. It belongs to the Oriental Orthodox family, with the Coptic, Armenian and Syriac churches. "Tewahedo" means "made one", for its belief that Christ has a single united nature, which is why it rejected the Council of Chalcedon in 451.

Christianity became the faith of the kings of Aksum in the 300s (Aksum adopts Christianity), when King Ezana was converted by Frumentius, a Syrian Christian whom the patriarch of Alexandria made the first bishop. For about sixteen centuries after that, the head of the Ethiopian church was an Egyptian monk sent from Alexandria. Monks from the eastern Roman world spread the faith in the countryside and translated the Bible into Ge'ez, written in the Ge'ez script, still the language of worship.

The church shaped the Ethiopian Empire. Saint Yared is credited with its sacred music. King Lalibela had the rock-hewn churches carved around 1200, and Emperor Zara Yaqob in the 1400s enforced church reforms across the realm. Every church holds a tabot, a copy of the tablets of the Ark of the Covenant, which tradition says rests in Aksum. Long fasts, a Saturday and Sunday Sabbath and food rules set it apart.

In the 1620s an emperor converted to Catholicism, but revolts forced the Jesuits out. The church finally got its own patriarch in 1959.
